introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus. Hosea gives us God's own words of tender love for his people: My heart is turned within me. Paul prays that we may know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge. In the Gospel, a soldier pierces the side of Jesus on the cross, and blood and water flow out. Let us draw near to the heart of Christ, the source of mercy and of life.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the heart of Christ was opened for us on the cross. Let us bring our prayers to the Father with trust.
intentions: For the Church, born from the pierced side of Christ: that she may be a sign of God's tender love for every person. Let us pray to the Lord.
For priests, on this day of prayer for their sanctification: that they may have hearts like the heart of Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose hearts are broken by grief, betrayal or loneliness: that they may find rest in the heart of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have wandered far from God: that they may discover that his love has never given them up. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be rooted and grounded in love, and love others with a gentle and humble heart. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, in the pierced heart of your Son you open for us the treasures of your love. Fill us with that love, and make our hearts like his. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The heart of God
reflection.body:
Some of the most tender words in the Bible are in today's first reading. God speaks of Israel as a child he raised: "I taught Ephraim to walk. I took them by their arms." He describes himself like a parent who lifts a child to the cheek: "I bent down to him and I fed him." Even when Israel turns away, God cannot bring himself to abandon them: "How can I give you up, Ephraim?... My heart is turned within me, my compassion is aroused."

The devotion to the Sacred Heart is a way of saying that this heart of God has taken human flesh in Jesus. His heart beat with human love: for his mother, his friends, the crowds, sinners.

In the Gospel, after Jesus has died, a soldier makes sure of his death: "one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out." John insists that he saw it himself. The Church has long seen in that blood and water the sacraments of the Eucharist and Baptism, and in the opened side the birth of the Church.

Paul prays for us on our knees, that we may be "rooted and grounded in love" and "know Christ's love which surpasses knowledge." This love is not something we can fully understand; we can only receive it and be filled.

The Gospel acclamation gives us the invitation of Jesus himself: "Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls." This week, bring the heavy things of your heart to Jesus in prayer, and ask him to make your heart gentle and humble like his.
